newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banks, miners boost Australia stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: Banks, miners boost Australia stocks by close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed higher on Thursday, keeping a firm grasp on early gains as the major miners and the big banks led the way higher.
By the close, the All Ordinaries index added 20.6 points to 2273.4.

Turnover was strong, driven by September series options expiry, several large companies going ex-dividend, and some position shuffling ahead of the September share price index futures close-out on Monday.
Despite the jostling for position as derivatives expired, brokers said plenty of solid buying interest remained.
"There is real buying out there with some big money being thrown at the market," said Derek Bond, director at Brisbane-based brokerage, Burrell and Co.
"The resources are up across the board and banks are finding support at their new highs. It's looking reasonably strong."

A juicy dividend yield was the main lure for buyers increasing their exposure to the banks, with both ANZ Bank and National Australia Bank reaching record highs of A$7.19 and A$13.21 respectively, while Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts continued to find investor favour, rising 1.8 percent to A$7.43.
Growth prospects, especially for its U.S. pallet business, was the fuel for a surge to a record high of A$20.50 for shares in transport and logistics group Brambles Industries.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to four, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
